title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Ten named Sacramento State spaces for studying, meeting, recreation, making, and taking a quiet break between classes.

cards.title: University Library
cards.subtitle: Library building
cards.notes: Use the library as a planned study stop: bring a task list, then ask at a service desk when you need help locating research support.
cards.short_summary: A central academic building with research and student-support services.
cards.evidence_claim: Sacramento State identifies the University Library as a campus landmark and lists it among academic buildings operating 8 a.m.–10 p.m. in its campus addendum.
cards.source_title: Campus Addendum to the Interim CSU Systemwide Time, Place and Manner Policy
cards.access_notes: Campus policy lists academic-building operating hours; confirm library service hours before a visit.

cards.title: StingerStudio Makerspace
cards.subtitle: University Library, Room 1529
cards.notes: Plan a making session around a project need, and check in with library staff for current equipment access or scheduled workshops.
cards.short_summary: A library makerspace for hands-on creative and project work.
cards.evidence_claim: Sacramento State lists StingerStudio Makerspace in Library Room 1529, next to the Carlsen Center.
cards.access_notes: The university page lists weekday service hours; verify availability and any equipment requirements before going.

cards.title: Student Research Center
cards.subtitle: University Library, Room 2026
cards.notes: Bring a draft question, outline, or citation problem so a research-support visit can focus quickly on the next step in your project.
cards.short_summary: A named library location for student research support.
cards.evidence_claim: Sacramento State lists the Student Research Center in Library Room 2026 and publishes its weekday hours.
cards.access_notes: University-listed hours vary by day; check the current schedule before visiting.

cards.title: Peer and Academic Resource Center
cards.subtitle: University Library, Room 4026
cards.notes: Use this stop to plan tutoring or peer academic support; arrive with the course, assignment, and a specific question ready to discuss.
cards.evidence_claim: Sacramento State lists the Peer and Academic Resource Center (PARC) in Library Room 4026 and publishes weekday hours.
cards.access_notes: Check the published weekday schedule and any appointment or drop-in details before arrival.

cards.title: Academic Information Resource Center
cards.subtitle: AIRC
cards.notes: Choose the AIRC when you need a long study window, then keep your campus ID and course materials handy for building access.
cards.short_summary: An academic building with extended student study access during fall and spring.
cards.evidence_claim: Sacramento State states that the Academic Information Resource Center is open 24 hours daily for student and staff study during fall and spring semesters.
cards.source_title: Campus Addendum to the Interim CSU Systemwide Time, Place and Manner Policy
cards.access_notes: The 24-hour study access is specified for fall and spring semesters; access may differ at other times.

cards.title: University Union
cards.subtitle: Campus gathering and services building
cards.notes: Use the Union as a practical meet-up point before an event or student-organization meeting, and consult the information desk for wayfinding.
cards.short_summary: A campus-life building with programs, services, and shared gathering space.
cards.evidence_claim: Sacramento State says the University Union and The WELL provide environments where students and others participate in campus life.
cards.access_notes: The campus addendum classifies the Union as limited-access space and publishes operating hours; reservations may be required for activities.

cards.title: Games Room
cards.subtitle: University Union, first floor
cards.notes: Build in a short recreational break between classes, and check the Union’s current desk information for activity availability that day.
cards.short_summary: A named first-floor University Union recreation space.
cards.evidence_claim: Sacramento State lists the Games Room on the first floor of the University Union and publishes weekday hours.
cards.access_notes: The university page lists Monday–Friday hours; verify current operations before visiting.

cards.title: University Union Gallery
cards.subtitle: University Union, second floor
cards.notes: Check the gallery’s current exhibition before heading upstairs, then allow time to view the work at a comfortable, unhurried pace.
cards.short_summary: A named second-floor gallery space in the University Union.
cards.evidence_claim: Sacramento State identifies the University Union Gallery as being on the second floor of the University Union.
cards.access_notes: Hours and exhibitions can change; confirm the current gallery schedule before visiting.

cards.title: The WELL
cards.subtitle: Student recreation and wellness facility
cards.notes: Plan a recreation or wellness visit around your schedule, and review current facility guidance before using activity areas or services.
cards.short_summary: A campus facility supporting recreation, wellness, and participation in campus life.
cards.evidence_claim: Sacramento State says The WELL’s programs, services, and facilities foster personal growth, healthy decision-making, and social interaction.
cards.access_notes: The campus addendum lists facility operating hours and notes that reservations may be required for activities.

cards.title: Library Quad
cards.subtitle: Outdoor lawn by the Library
cards.notes: Use this outdoor landmark for a daylight reset or a planned group meet-up, while keeping paths clear and respecting any reserved activity.
cards.short_summary: A named campus lawn space beside the library area.
cards.evidence_claim: Sacramento State identifies Library Quad as an outdoor lawn space and names it in campus policy for permitted outdoor activity.
cards.source_title: Campus Addendum to the Interim CSU Systemwide Time, Place and Manner Policy
cards.access_notes: Campus policy lists this as public outdoor lawn space during stated hours; events or other uses may require reservation.
